1.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Verify scene safety first, then triage victims by checking breathing under 30 per minute, pulse perfusion under 2 seconds, and mental status.
core_mechanism_bullets: 1. Scene Safety & BSI Gloves: Stop and survey for live wires, traffic, fire, or gas before touching any patient; put on nitrile gloves.
2. Walking Wounded -> GREEN (Minor): Direct everyone who can walk to move to a safe collection zone for secondary assessment.
3. Airway, Breathing (>30/min) -> RED: Open airway if not breathing; respiratory rate over 30/min or radial pulse absent marks IMMEDIATE (Red).
4. Stable Vitals -> YELLOW (Delayed): Breathing under 30/min, capillary refill under 2 seconds, and obeys simple commands marks DELAYED.
1.worked_field_example: A conscious hiker breathing 22 times per minute with a 1-second capillary refill and an ankle fracture receives a Yellow Delayed tag.
1.counselor_tabletop_demo: Lay out the four color-coded START triage tags (Red, Yellow, Green, Black) and classify three wilderness injury scenarios in under 60 seconds.
1.real_world_connection_box: US HHS CHEMM & CERT START Field Standard: Verify scene safety first, then triage victims by checking breathing under 30 per minute, pulse perfusion under 2 seconds, and mental status.
1.grounded_citation_label: Verified: Scouting America Pamphlet + US HHS CHEMM / CERT START Protocol
1.bespoke_visual_caption: Emergency triage field layout pairing Red, Yellow, Green, and Black priority tags with a stethoscope, trauma shears, nitrile gloves, and first-aid kit.

2.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Cool thermal burns gently with clean running water for 10 to 20 minutes and never pop blisters or apply ice or butter.
core_mechanism_bullets: Superficial (1st Degree): Epidermis: Red, dry, painful skin without blisters; cool with running tap water for 10+ minutes.
Partial-Thickness (2nd Degree): Dermis: Swollen, wet, intensely painful fluid blisters; keep blisters intact and apply loose dry sterile gauze.
Full-Thickness (3rd Degree): Subcutis: Charred, leathery, or pearly white tissue with nerve damage; call 911 and treat for shock.
Chemical & Electrical Burns (911): Brush dry powder first before 20-min water flush; electrical burns require cardiac evaluation for internal injury.
2.worked_field_example: A red, blistered forearm scald from camp stove water is a partial-thickness second-degree burn requiring cool running water and loose sterile gauze.
2.counselor_tabletop_demo: Trace the epidermis, dermis, and subcutaneous layers on the skin cutaway to show why intact blisters protect underlying dermis from infection.
2.real_world_connection_box: American Burn Association & Red Cross Standard: Cool thermal burns gently with clean running water for 10 to 20 minutes and never pop blisters or apply ice or butter.
2.grounded_citation_label: Verified: Scouting America Pamphlet + American Burn Association & Red Cross
2.bespoke_visual_caption: Anatomical cross-section of human skin illustrating epidermis, dermis, and subcutaneous tissue layers for classifying burn depth.
2.v47_slide_title: American Burn Association & Red Cross Standard
v47_primary_source_bullets: Cool thermal burns gently with clean running water for 10 to 20 minutes and never pop blisters or apply ice or butter.

3.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Cool thermal burns gently with clean running water for 10 to 20 minutes and never pop blisters or apply ice or butter.
core_mechanism_bullets: Step 1: Call 911 & Glove Up: Activate EMS immediately and send a runner for a trauma kit and AED if patient is unresponsive.
Step 2: Firm Two-Hand Direct Pressure: Press sterile gauze firmly with both hands continuously for at least 5 minutes without peeking.
Step 3: Add Layers, Never Strip Clots: If blood soaks through the first pad, stack fresh gauze directly on top so forming fibrin clots stay intact.
Step 4: Windlass Tourniquet (Extremity): Strap 2 to 3 inches proximal to limb wound, twist rod until bright red bleeding stops, and write exact time (T=HH:MM).
3.worked_field_example: A red, blistered forearm scald from camp stove water is a partial-thickness second-degree burn requiring cool running water and loose sterile gauze.
3.counselor_tabletop_demo: Trace the epidermis, dermis, and subcutaneous layers on the skin cutaway to show why intact blisters protect underlying dermis from infection.

primary_source_citation.title: American Heart Association (AHA) Technical Reference: Cardiac Chain of Survival: High-Quality CPR & AED Sequence

4.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Apply firm direct pressure with sterile gauze pads first to control extremity bleeding.
core_mechanism_bullets: Link 1: Recognize Cardiac Arrest & 911: Unresponsive patient with absent or gasping agonal breaths; call 911 on speakerphone and fetch AED.
Link 2: High-Quality Chest Compressions: 100 to 120 BPM on lower half of sternum, 2.0 to 2.4 in depth, full recoil, 30:2 rescue breath ratio.
Link 3: Rapid AED Pad Placement: Upper-right chest below collarbone and lower-left ribs; yell CLEAR before analysis and shock delivery.
Link 4: Resume Compressions Immediately: Restart chest compressions within 2 seconds after shock delivery until EMS paramedics assume care.
4.worked_field_example: For bright red spurting bleeding on the mid-forearm, place the tourniquet 2 inches above the wound and twist the windlass until bleeding stops.
4.counselor_tabletop_demo: Practice three-stage hemorrhage control on a foam arm trainer using direct gauze pressure, a pressure wrap, and a windlass tourniquet.
4.real_world_connection_box: ACS Stop the Bleed & CoTCCC Field Standard: Apply firm direct pressure with sterile gauze pads first to control extremity bleeding. For life-threatening arterial limb bleeding, secure a windlass tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the wound and never over a joint.
4.grounded_citation_label: Verified: Scouting America Pamphlet + ACS Stop the Bleed & CoTCCC
4.bespoke_visual_caption: Three-stage bleeding control sequence showing direct sterile gauze pressure, an elastic pressure wrap, and a locked windlass tourniquet.
4.v47_slide_title: ACS Stop the Bleed & CoTCCC Field Standard
v47_primary_source_bullets: Apply firm direct pressure with sterile gauze pads first to control extremity bleeding.
